findings.remediation: Use yaml.safe_load or an explicitly selected SafeLoader/CSafeLoader.
findings.review: Check the installed PyYAML version and loader. Some modern versions reject a missing Loader instead of loading.

findings.title: Dynamic SQL statement
findings.message: A database-like API receives a dynamically built statement; parameter binding needs review.
findings.remediation: Use driver placeholders and pass values separately. Allowlist any dynamic table or column identifiers.
findings.review: Confirm this is a database API and determine whether any part of the statement is externally controlled.

findings.title: Input influences a filesystem path
findings.message: Input contributes to a filesystem path; containment requires review.
findings.remediation: Resolve paths under a fixed allowed directory, enforce containment and consider symlink races; prefer opaque file IDs.
findings.review: Check the operation, allowed base directory, authorization and any validation before filesystem access.

limitations: Findings are review candidates, not proof of exploitability. No findings does not mean the application is secure.
Python analysis is bounded and intraprocedural. It does not resolve calls across functions or files, or prove sanitizers correct.
JavaScript/TypeScript and configuration checks use lexical heuristics, not a full parser or data-flow engine.
PHP, Java, C#, Go and Ruby receive navigation hotspots only. Callable identity, reachability and function scope may be unresolved.
Unsupported languages receive limited secret checks only. Dependency, vendored, minified and generated code is excluded by default.
No live CVE lookup, dependency resolution, runtime testing, authorization verification or automatic exploitation is performed.
manual_review: Authorization: verify object ownership, tenant isolation and role checks on every sensitive operation.
Authentication: review account recovery, MFA, session rotation, token expiry and revocation.
Business logic: review payment amounts, state transitions, concurrency and abuse limits.
Web controls: review CSRF, CORS, cookie settings, security headers and output encoding by context.
Files and network: verify upload limits, destination allowlists, path containment and egress policy.
Dependencies: use a maintained advisory scanner against resolved lockfiles; inventory here is not a CVE audit.
Deployment: review production configuration, IAM permissions, secret rotation and audit logging.
